notes: Counts: 45 real, 45 fake; all anchors unique so the two-per-anchor cap is satisfied. Real decades span 1963-2019. All 45 real titles are ones I am >=95% sure exist; verified from model knowledge only, no live database check was run in this environment. Reveal-level facts worth spot-checking at import (existence is certain, the anecdote is the softer claim): The Sting II's Oscar score nomination, The Net 2.0 being directed by Charles Winkler (son of the original's director Irwin Winkler), the Smokey and the Bandit Part 3 'Gleason as both roles' early-cut story, and the Mrs. Doubtfire 2 in-development claim used in a fake's reveal. For fakes, I checked each invented title against known filmographies and known announced-but-unmade projects; at import, run the 45 fake titles against your TMDB/OMDb catalog to confirm zero exact-title matches, paying attention to plain-numbered ones (Sinister 3, My Girl 3, Clueless 2, Old School 2, Weird Science 2, Baby's Day Out 2) and The Bodyguard 2, whose base title is used by unrelated Thai and Hong Kong films. Items are ordered real-then-fake; shuffle before serving.

items.title: Savage Sam
items.reveal: Disney really made a sequel about Old Yeller's son, released six years after they shot the dog.

items.title: Look What's Happened to Rosemary's Baby
items.reveal: ABC aired this TV sequel with Patty Duke taking over the Mia Farrow role and the baby now a grown man.

items.title: Oliver's Story
items.reveal: Ryan O'Neal returned for a sequel about Oliver dating again after Jenny's death, and it flopped.

items.title: The Bad News Bears Go to Japan
items.reveal: The third Bears film sends the team to Tokyo with Tony Curtis as their hustler promoter.

items.title: Butch and Sundance: The Early Days
items.anchor: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
items.reveal: A prequel with Tom Berenger and William Katt in the Newman and Redford roles.

items.title: More American Graffiti
items.reveal: The sequel scatters the cast across Vietnam, drag strips, and Haight-Ashbury, with storylines shot in different aspect ratios.

items.title: Grease 2
items.reveal: Michelle Pfeiffer's first lead role; almost nobody from the original returned except Frenchy and the teachers.

items.title: Trail of the Pink Panther
items.reveal: Released two years after Peter Sellers died, it stars him anyway, assembled from outtakes.

items.title: The Sting II
items.reveal: Jackie Gleason and Mac Davis replaced Newman and Redford, and it still landed an Oscar nomination for its score.

items.title: Staying Alive
items.reveal: The Saturday Night Fever sequel was written and directed by Sylvester Stallone.

items.title: Smokey and the Bandit Part 3
items.reveal: Burt Reynolds appears only in a cameo; an early cut reportedly had Jackie Gleason playing both Smokey and the Bandit.

items.title: Return to Oz
items.reveal: Disney's sequel opens with Dorothy being sent for electroshock therapy.

items.title: The Parent Trap II
items.reveal: Hayley Mills played both twins again in a TV sequel 25 years after the original.

items.title: Teen Wolf Too
items.reveal: Jason Bateman replaced Michael J. Fox as the wolf's cousin, who boxes instead of playing basketball.

items.title: Caddyshack II
items.reveal: Jackie Mason stepped in for Rodney Dangerfield; Chevy Chase and the gopher were the main returnees.

items.title: Splash, Too
items.reveal: Disney made a TV sequel with a different actor in every role, including the mermaid.

items.title: The Two Jakes
items.reveal: Jack Nicholson directed himself in the Chinatown sequel.

items.title: Omen IV: The Awakening
items.reveal: The fourth Omen is a TV movie about Damien's daughter.

items.title: Weekend at Bernie's II
items.reveal: Voodoo partially reanimates the corpse, which can only walk when calypso music plays.

items.title: The Birds II: Land's End
items.reveal: The made-for-TV Hitchcock sequel's director took his name off it and is credited as Alan Smithee.

items.title: The NeverEnding Story III
items.reveal: A young Jack Black plays the bully who leads a gang called the Nasties.

items.title: Blues Brothers 2000
items.reveal: John Goodman fills the John Belushi slot and the band adds a ten-year-old.

items.title: The Rage: Carrie 2
items.reveal: Amy Irving returned as Sue Snell, the only link to the 1976 original, 23 years later.

items.title: Book of Shadows: Blair Witch 2
items.reveal: The studio recut it so heavily that its director, a respected documentarian, disowned the result.

items.title: Cruel Intentions 2
items.reveal: It began as a failed TV prequel pilot and was stitched into a direct-to-video movie.

items.title: American Psycho 2
items.reveal: Mila Kunis plays a student who killed Patrick Bateman as a child, a premise she has since said she regrets.

items.title: Home Alone 4: Taking Back the House
items.reveal: A TV movie that recast every single role, including Kevin.

items.title: Christmas Vacation 2: Cousin Eddie's Island Adventure
items.reveal: A TV sequel in which Randy Quaid's Cousin Eddie is the lead and the Griswolds barely appear.

items.title: Dumb and Dumberer: When Harry Met Lloyd
items.reveal: A prequel with new actors as teenage Harry and Lloyd; the Farrelly brothers had nothing to do with it.

items.title: Dirty Dancing: Havana Nights
items.reveal: A 1958 Cuba retelling in which Patrick Swayze cameos as a dance instructor.

items.title: Carlito's Way: Rise to Power
items.reveal: A direct-to-video prequel with Jay Hernandez in the Al Pacino role.

items.title: Son of the Mask
items.reveal: Jamie Kennedy replaced Jim Carrey and a baby gets the mask's powers.

items.title: Single White Female 2: The Psycho
items.reveal: The subtitle is literally The Psycho, and it went straight to video 13 years later with no returning cast.

items.title: The Net 2.0
items.reveal: The straight-to-DVD sequel was directed by the son of the man who directed the original.

items.title: Road House 2: Last Call
items.reveal: The straight-to-DVD sequel arrived 17 years later with none of the original cast.

items.title: Bachelor Party 2: The Last Temptation
items.reveal: The Tom Hanks comedy got an unrated direct-to-DVD sequel 24 years later.

items.title: S. Darko
items.reveal: A sequel following Donnie's little sister Samantha; Richard Kelly had no involvement.

items.title: Ace Ventura Jr.: Pet Detective
items.reveal: A kids' TV movie about Ace's son; Jim Carrey is nowhere in it.

items.title: Legally Blondes
items.reveal: A direct-to-DVD spinoff about Elle's British twin cousins, produced by Reese Witherspoon, who does not appear.

items.title: Mean Girls 2
items.reveal: A made-for-TV sequel whose only returning character is Principal Duvall.

items.title: A Christmas Story 2
items.reveal: An official direct-to-video sequel with Daniel Stern as the Old Man.

items.title: Jarhead 2: Field of Fire
items.reveal: The Sam Mendes war drama got a straight-to-video action sequel with an unrelated cast, then two more.

items.title: Jingle All the Way 2
items.reveal: Larry the Cable Guy took over the Schwarzenegger role in a WWE Studios production.

items.title: Kindergarten Cop 2
items.reveal: Dolph Lundgren teaches the kindergarten this time, direct to video.

items.title: Backdraft 2
items.reveal: It arrived 28 years later, straight to video, with William Baldwin back.

items.title: Ghost 2: Unfinished Business
items.reveal: Ghost never got a sequel; the subtitle borrows the film's own premise, which is exactly what a real DTV sequel would do.

items.title: Top Gun: Afterburner
items.reveal: The only real sequel is Maverick; Afterburner is just the right amount of jet jargon.

items.title: Speed 3: Flatline
items.reveal: The franchise stopped at Cruise Control; a Speed 3 exists only as a Father Ted joke.

items.title: Con Air 2: Final Descent
items.reveal: Con Air never got a sequel, though every part of this title sounds like it did.

items.title: Air Force One: Retaliation
items.reveal: No sequel exists; the closest real title is the unrelated 2024 movie Air Force One Down.

items.title: The Fugitive: Dead Run
items.reveal: The real follow-up is U.S. Marshals, which dropped both Harrison Ford and the title.

items.title: Panic Room 2: Home Invasion
items.reveal: The Fincher film has no sequel; the subtitle is the entire genre.

items.title: Fatal Attraction 2: Obsession
items.reveal: No film sequel exists, only a 2023 TV series.

items.title: The Hand That Rocks the Cradle 2: A Family Affair
items.anchor: The Hand That Rocks the Cradle
items.reveal: No sequel exists; the title copies the real Single White Female 2 formula exactly.

items.title: Flashdance 2: Steel City Nights
items.reveal: Flashdance has no sequel; Steel City is Pittsburgh, which is the kind of homework a DTV subtitle does.

items.title: Footloose: The Next Step
items.reveal: No sequel exists, just a 2011 remake.

items.title: Coyote Ugly 2: Last Dance
items.reveal: A sequel was reported to be in development and never appeared.

items.title: The Bodyguard 2: Never Let Go
items.reveal: The Costner film has no sequel; unrelated Asian action movies have used the base title.

items.title: Pretty Woman: Ever After
items.reveal: No sequel exists; Garry Marshall reunited the leads in Runaway Bride instead.

items.title: Sweet Home Alabama 2: Southern Vows
items.reveal: No sequel was ever made despite years of sequel talk.

items.title: Clueless 2: Back in Session
items.reveal: Clueless got a TV series and a musical, never a film sequel.

items.title: 10 Things I Hate About You Too
items.reveal: The 'Too' construction is stolen from Teen Wolf Too, which is real; this one is not.

items.title: She's All That 2: Prom Queen
items.reveal: The franchise's only follow-up is the gender-swapped remake He's All That.

items.title: Old School 2: Homecoming
items.reveal: A sequel was talked about for years and never made.

items.title: EuroTrip 2: Winter Break
items.reveal: EuroTrip flopped in theaters and thrived on DVD, exactly where a sequel would have lived; none exists.

items.title: Liar Liar 2: Truth Be Told
items.reveal: Jim Carrey hits really did spawn Carrey-less DTV sequels, but Liar Liar was spared.

items.title: Mrs. Doubtfire 2: The Nanny Returns
items.reveal: A real sequel was in development before Robin Williams died; it never got this far.

items.title: Matilda 2: The New Girl
items.reveal: Matilda's only follow-up is the musical; no DTV sequel exists.

items.title: Homeward Bound III: Lost in the Rockies
items.reveal: The series stopped at Lost in San Francisco; the third trip is invented.

items.title: Cool Runnings 2: Back on Ice
items.reveal: Disney never made one, despite making sequels to far smaller hits in that era.

items.title: Little Giants 2: Away Game
items.reveal: No sequel exists; Away Game is the standard kids-sports-sequel subtitle.

items.title: Rookie of the Year 2: The Big Leagues
items.reveal: No sequel exists; the title just follows the real Sandlot sequel formula.

items.title: Varsity Blues 2: The Comeback
items.reveal: No sequel was ever made.

items.title: Sinister 3
items.reveal: Sinister 2 is real; a third was discussed and never happened.

items.title: Arachnophobia 2: The Nest
items.reveal: The original has no sequel, only a long-rumored remake.

items.title: Scarface: The Beginning
items.reveal: Carlito's Way really got a DTV prequel exactly like this; Scarface did not.

items.title: Training Day 2: Graduation Day
items.reveal: The follow-up was a 2017 CBS series, never a film.

items.title: The Goonies: Return to Astoria
items.reveal: Decades of sequel rumors produced an NES game and nothing else.

items.title: Twister: Eye of the Storm
items.reveal: The real sequel waited 28 years and is called Twisters.

items.title: Poltergeist IV: The Reckoning
items.reveal: The series stopped at III in 1988, plus a remake; a fourth exists only here.

items.title: Weird Science 2
items.reveal: It became a TV series instead; there is no film sequel.

items.title: Ferris Bueller's Day Off 2
items.reveal: No sequel exists; the closest thing is a Super Bowl ad Broderick did in character.

items.title: Turner & Hooch 2: New Tricks
items.reveal: The follow-up was a 2021 Disney+ series; the dog never got a film sequel.

items.title: The Pacifier 2: Basic Training
items.reveal: No sequel exists; the Vin Diesel family comedy stayed a one-off.

items.title: Snow Dogs 2: Race to the Pole
items.reveal: Disney made sequels to much smaller hits, but not this one.

items.title: My Girl 3
items.reveal: My Girl 2 is real; the third one is not.

items.title: Baby's Day Out 2
items.reveal: A theatrical flop that thrived on video is exactly the profile that got sequels; this one didn't.

items.title: The Waterboy 2: Overtime
items.reveal: Sandler never made one, though Happy Gilmore eventually got its real sequel.

items.title: What Lies Beneath 2: Still Waters
items.reveal: The Zemeckis thriller has no sequel; the subtitle is standard DTV water metaphor.

items.title: The Wedding Planner 2: The Honeymoon
items.reveal: No sequel exists; Jennifer Lopez rom-coms never got the DTV treatment.
